A_general.release_status: Varies by endpoint: Genie One is GA; system.ai.dbsql, system.ai.sandbox and system.ai.web_search are in Unity Gateway Beta; Genie Agent and AI Search workspace endpoints are Public Preview.
other_official_servers: Databricks-provided workspace MCP family includes system.ai.genie_one_mcp, system.ai.dbsql, system.ai.web_search, system.ai.sandbox and external-service connectors such as system.ai.github and system.ai.slack.

Separate workspace endpoints include Genie Agent (/api/2.0/mcp/genie/{genie_space_id}), AI Search (/api/2.0/mcp/ai-search/{catalog}/{schema}/{index_name}), Databricks SQL (/api/2.0/mcp/sql), and Unity Catalog functions (/api/2.0/mcp/functions/{catalog}/{schema}/{function_name}).
The former Beta /api/2.0/mcp/genie endpoint is deprecated; Databricks states it will be sunset on October 31, 2026.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP access price was found. Databricks documents underlying service charges: Genie One MCP uses Chat in Genie One pricing; Genie Agent uses Databricks SQL pricing; SQL and AI Search endpoints use their respective product pricing.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Databricks publishes product and compute pricing; no fixed price is stated on the cited product pricing page.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Underlying compute or product usage applies. Unity Catalog functions use serverless general compute pricing, Databricks SQL MCP uses Databricks SQL pricing, and AI Search indexes use AI Search pricing.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The workspace URL is customer-specific. Unity Gateway system.ai MCPs require the relevant service to be enabled; system.ai.dbsql, system.ai.sandbox and system.ai.web_search require an account admin to enable the Unity Gateway Beta preview. Workspace MCP endpoints require a workspace admin to enable Managed MCP Servers. Access is also subject to the underlying resource permissions. system.ai.web_search is unavailable in HIPAA/BAA workspaces and has region/cross-Geo restrictions; system.ai.sandbox has no network egress.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and Databricks account/workspace administrators; resource owners control underlying grants and permissions.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tool effects vary: Genie One asks questions, returns query results, and can cancel turns; SQL permits reads and writes by default, configurable to read-only; Genie Agent is documented read-only; AI Search is retrieval. No hosted tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were found. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow is documented. Unity Gateway policies can restrict calls; user/client confirmation is not equivalent to server enforcement. 3. Access uses OAuth scopes and caller/resource permissions. Genie One recommends on-behalf-of user OAuth and also supports service principals. Gateway services support grants/policies; workspace endpoints bypass Gateway governance. No public metadata, token lifetime, or revocation details were available for the unspecified workspace. 4. Endpoint variants include Unity Gateway and legacy workspace routes; Gateway calls can be restricted with grants and policies. SQL has a read-only policy setting; SQL warehouse and AI Search parameters can be preset via _meta. Workspace endpoints require preview enablement and bypass Gateway policies/traces. 5. Genie One and workspace query services enforce Unity Catalog permissions. AI Search excludes internal columns beginning __ by default; no generalized PII masking documented. 6. Genie query results are truncated, including full-result retrieval when a size limit is exceeded; SQL truncates large results. AI Search supports num_results; no universal rate, quota, or per-call cap identified. Pricing follows underlying service. 7. The pages document typed/configuration parameters and valid AI Search query_type values; hosted validation/correction behavior for unknown arguments or operator overrides is not documented. 8. Gateway traffic has tracing/usage governance; endpoints bypassing Gateway do not appear in its tracing tables. Hosted MCP telemetry payload, retention, and opt-out were not identified. 9. No vendor feedback, rating, survey, or reporting tool appears in the official lists reviewed. Genie One docs recommend Genie One for workspace natural-language analytics and prefer view_ask when available; these are documentation instructions. No upsell response found. 10. No server-delivered skill tool or initialize instructions found. Databricks separately documents adding skills to coding agents; that is outside the listed MCP actions. 11. Genie One supports conversation_id follow-ups. Genie Agent endpoint explicitly does not pass conversation history to Genie. 12. Non-standard service family: separate MCP endpoints expose different tool sets; Unity Gateway fronts governed system.ai services. Genie One also runs a Databricks agent internally. 13. execute_sql is a SQL execution tool, a broad query interface. The reviewed official docs do not describe a generic raw HTTP or script execution tool on these named endpoints; system.ai.sandbox separately runs Python, SQL, or shell code in an isolated environment without network egress.

E_aggregated.action_count: 6 named tools across Genie One and SQL documentation, plus configuration-dependent AI Search tool(s); Genie Agent tool name is not published
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The input is a workspace-level placeholder, not a uniquely selected MCP endpoint. Official tool lists exist for Genie One (5 names: genie_ask, genie_poll_response, genie_get_query_result, genie_cancel_response, view_ask) and Databricks SQL (execute_sql appears in the official example). AI Search has dynamic per-index tool names; its official example gives a placeholder name, and Genie Agent docs publish no tool name. actions.json records all six fixed official names plus the documented AI Search name pattern. No catalogue-only actions were added. Claude's third-party Databricks Genie connector directory lists four Genie tools and omits the official view_ask; it describes the Genie One connector and does not establish the selected workspace endpoint. Composio's page is its Databricks API toolkit, not evidence of this MCP endpoint's tool list.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Genie One guidance says to wait for the prior poll call and explains how to use query-result retrieval after truncation. AI Search examples advise setting a three-result cap and search filters via _meta. These are client configuration and agent guidance; the sources do not establish that every caller is forced to use those example values.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Databricks states “Unity Catalog permissions are always enforced, so users and agents can only query data they're allowed to access.” Gateway-governed services support grants and policies. The docs also state that workspace endpoint calls bypass Unity Gateway tracing, MCP grants, policies, and guardrails.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Genie One answers are grounded in Genie Ontology and include deep links to Databricks sources; supporting clients may render progress, visualizations, and results in an interactive View. Databricks recommends on-behalf-of user authentication for data governance and clickthrough.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission enforcement is documented for Genie One, AI Search, Genie Agent, and SQL; Unity Gateway provides centralized grants/policies for its managed services. For legacy workspace endpoints, docs explicitly say Gateway policies and tracing do not apply. Result truncation is described as server behavior. No public hosted code was found to independently verify these claims.

contradictions: The official Genie One tool reference lists five tools, while Claude's third-party Databricks Genie connector lists four and omits view_ask. The official list takes precedence.

The default /api/2.0/mcp/genie workspace endpoint is described as deprecated, while the current Genie One endpoint is /ai-gateway/mcp-services/system.ai.genie_one_mcp and uses the ai-gateway scope rather than genie.

The input identifies only a workspace-level endpoint, but official documentation distinguishes multiple MCP services with different tool sets, scopes, release states, and governance. An exact per-endpoint action count therefore cannot be resolved.
observations_for_research: Databricks exposes services through multiple workspace-specific routes, with some routed through Unity Gateway and others bypassing it.
The same product area offers both natural-language agent-mediated analytics and direct SQL execution; the documented governance and write behavior differ by endpoint.
Tool availability can be configuration-dependent: AI Search names tools per index, while Unity Catalog functions and other resources can be reached through separately scoped MCP endpoints.
